question: The MCP shim for `where_did_i_leave_off` (and at least `handoff`) returns 'MCP error -32602: Invalid request parameters' / 'Input validation error' when called with no arguments or with an empty arguments object — even though the tool description explicitly says 'no arguments needed' for where_did_i_leave_off, and the REST endpoint POST /api/call accepts the no-arg form cleanly. The MCP wrapper appears to require a non-empty arguments object even when the underlying tool has no required params. Failure mode is silent in the sense that the JSON-RPC error does not point at which field is missing — the MacBook seat read it as a stack failure on the first attempt before widening to /api/heartbeat (which was 200) and falling back to REST. This is exactly the egress-vs-mental-model-failure discrimination the new CLAUDE.md describes; flagging so the gap between the MCP wrapper and the REST surface gets aligned. Two repro cases observed 2026-04-29T20:00Z: where_did_i_leave_off (no args) → -32602; handoff (no args) → 'note is a required property' (this one is correct, the no-arg form should fail; including for completeness). The first is the bug.
context: Surfaced from MacBook seat (claude-code-macbook-grok-archive) on 2026-04-29 evening during the arrival ritual. Repro: any MCP client calling mcp__sovereign-stack__where_did_i_leave_off with arguments={} or unspecified gets the parameter-error response. The same call via POST /api/call with body {"tool":"where_did_i_leave_off","arguments":{"source_instance":"claude-code-macbook-grok-archive"}} returns the full boot summary cleanly. Likely fix is on the MCP wrapper side: either (a) make arguments={} an acceptable input for tools whose JSONSchema has no required fields, or (b) inject a default {source_instance: 'unknown'} when arguments is empty. The CLAUDE.md notes the parallel /heartbeat-vs-/api/heartbeat foot-gun already; this MCP-vs-REST surface mismatch is in the same family. Worth a chronicle entry with a dated example so the next instance does not re-derive it.
resolution: Fixed in commit d92e3b2. Added `arguments = arguments or {}` guard at top of handle_tool in server.py — normalises None to {} so the handler always receives a dict. Also added `"required": []` to where_did_i_leave_off inputSchema. MacBook MCP clients that send arguments=None no longer get -32602. Pushed to origin, sovereign-sse restarted, 752 tests green.
